data.name: Make It Rain: Love of Money
data.detailed_description:
Você é rápido? Não, sério... muito rápido???

Este é um jogo extremamente inteligente, muito simples, fácil, difícil e divertido ao mesmo tempo. Mas o que isso tudo significa? Bom, basta deslizar as notas e ver a quantia de dinheiro aumentando. São centenas, milhares, e logo, milhões, bilhões, em seguida, mega-bilhões e muito mais. Mas para conseguir isso tudo você vai ter que ser esperto na hora de investir!

Talvez você invista em capital de risco, agiotagem ou perfuração.

Talvez você monte uma banca de limonada, um cassino ou uma faculdade para palhaços.

Ou talvez você compre um juiz federal e apenas aproveite a grana que vai entrar!

Então deslize, deslize, deslize, deslize, deslize, deslize, deslize, deslize, deslize, deslize, deslize, deslize, deslize, deslize, deslize, deslize, deslize, deslize, deslize, deslize, deslize, deslize, deslize, deslize, deslize, deslize, deslize, deslize, deslize, deslize, deslize, deslize, deslize, deslize, deslize, deslize, deslize, deslize, deslize, deslize, deslize, deslize, deslize, deslize e abra caminho para a sua glória.

É um jogo idiota? Ou você está perdendo para o seus amigos e agora fica dando desculpas?

Ah, e não se esqueça de comprar um balde. Mesmo alguém tão animado e corajoso como você não vai conseguir ficar deslizando para sempre...

reviews.review:
Make It Rain: Love of Money is a very simple idle style game that is basically built around making as much virtual money as possible. I start by swiping bills across the screen and watching my cash pile up, then I use that money to unlock investments and improve how quickly I earn. The whole thing is intentionally ridiculous, with things like lemonade stands, casinos, offshore drilling and even shady investments being thrown into the mix. I like how quickly it gets to the point because I do not have to learn a complicated system before I can start making progress.

The swiping itself is probably the best part for me. It sounds silly, but there is something satisfying about repeatedly dragging the money across the screen and watching the numbers increase. The game also gives me more ways to make money as I progress, so eventually I am not relying entirely on manual swiping. Investments can keep producing income and I can focus on improving the systems that are already making me money. It gives the basic clicking idea just enough progression to stop it from being completely mindless.

I also like the ridiculous humour behind the whole thing. The game is clearly making fun of the obsession with getting richer, and it lets me build a completely stupid virtual fortune through increasingly questionable decisions. I can invest in things like venture capital and loan sharking, while other options involve more obviously shady behaviour. Eventually I can establish a legacy and pass my wealth on so that the next run starts with bonuses. That reset system gives the game a little more purpose because starting over is not simply losing everything for no reason.

The biggest problem is that the gameplay is extremely repetitive. Once I understand the basic loop, I am still swiping money, buying upgrades and waiting for my income to increase. There is not much room for complicated strategy, despite the investment theme making it sound like there might be. I can make choices about where to put my money, but the main goal is always the same. Get more money, increase the rate, unlock the next thing and repeat. It can be fun in short bursts, but I would struggle to sit with it for a long session.

The free to play design is also something I have mixed feelings about. The Steam version is free and includes in app purchases, so I can play the main game without paying, but there are clearly systems designed around spending as well. That does not completely ruin the experience for me, especially because the basic idea is already so simple, but it does make the progression feel less satisfying when I know there are ways to speed things up through purchases. I prefer when an idle game lets me enjoy the slow climb without making the faster route feel like something I am supposed to buy.

What I do appreciate is how easy it is to pick up and put down. I can play for a few minutes, make some investments, watch my income grow and then leave it alone. It is not trying to be a serious business simulator, and I think it works better once I stop expecting it to have any real depth. The ridiculous numbers and silly approach to capitalism are most of the appeal. I can see myself enjoying it when I want something mindless, especially when I only have a few minutes to spare.

Overall, Make It Rain: Love of Money is a decent little incremental game that understands the appeal of watching numbers get bigger. I like the satisfying swiping, silly investment options, automatic income and legacy system, and the humour gives the basic formula some personality. The main loop becomes repetitive very quickly and the free to play elements take away some of the satisfaction from the progression. For me, it is fun enough as a short distraction, but there is not enough depth here for me to rate it alongside my stronger idle games.

Rating: 6.7/10
